title: Inflation and appreciation
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest point, compound interest, teaches the general formula for growing money, while this point applies it to rising prices and asset values, which is a narrower application and not the same idea.

draft.title: Inflation and appreciation
card: a general rise in prices over time. A fixed yearly inflation rate makes prices grow like compound interest.
a rise in the value of an asset, such as a house, over time. A fixed yearly rate works the same way.
Use FV = PV(1 + r)ⁿ. PV is today's price or value, r is the yearly rate as a decimal, and n is the number of years. FV is the future price or value.
Example: a $4000 laptop with inflation of 3% a year. After 2 years, FV = 4000 × 1.03² = 4000 × 1.0609 = $4243.60.
draft.remember: Inflation and appreciation both use FV = PV(1 + r)ⁿ, with r as the yearly rate of increase.

a.q: A unit is worth $500 000 and appreciates by 4% a year. Which calculation gives its value after 3 years?
a.why: Appreciation of 4% means r = 0.04, so each year the value is multiplied by 1.04. After 3 years that is 1.04³. Multiplying by 1.12 treats the growth as simple, not compound, and ignores that each year builds on the last.
a.clue: Each year the value is multiplied by the same number.

b.q: A bus fare is $3.50 today. Inflation is 2% a year. What is the fare after 2 years, to the nearest cent?
b.why: FV = 3.50 × 1.02² = 3.50 × 1.0404 = 3.6414, which is $3.64. The answer $3.57 uses only one year of inflation, so it skips a step.
b.clue: Multiply by 1.02 once for each year.

check.summary: No problems found. The worked example, both questions and both explanations are correct and fit the card.
